correctness.rationale: All quantified block lengths k>=0 are treated by the digit-product identity and a one-line exact block-sum formula. An injectivity lemma for four integer-affine pair values reduces every potential triadic Abelian fourth power to a constant run of at least four signs, impossible by the substitution. The constructed constant run at positions 5..7 yields an Abelian cube for every 3^k. The same lemma gives both exhaustive cube-start cases. A direct transition-count recurrence proves existence of the limiting run density 1/6, and a digit recurrence gives the exact numerator C_k. The supplied verifier independently checks millions of finite instances and the length-seven contrast, but no infinite statement rests on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The closest same-word primary source (Meleshko et al., arXiv:2207.10171, §4.1) classifies pointwise pseudoperiod shift sets, not equal-Parikh consecutive block powers. The strongest directly relevant abelian-4 avoidance source (Currie et al., arXiv:2111.07857) constructs a different word, and cannot imply a theorem about this word, which demonstrably contains a period-seven abelian fourth power. Chen and Wen (arXiv:1809.06554) count Parikh classes for a different generalized Thue–Morse substitution, not the positionwise triadic exponent, complete cube-start classifier, or exact cube densities. Targeted web and mathematical-record searches found no matching statement. Residual risk of an unindexed equivalent remains.
residual_risks: Bibliographic search and available mathematical records cannot exclude an unindexed theorem equivalent to the triadic cube-start classification.

value.rationale: The Mephisto Waltz word is a standard automatic example with ordinary fourth-power-freeness; the Abelian version is strictly different, as an explicit nontriadic Abelian fourth power proves. Determining the sharp full set of exponents for every substitution-scale period, all cube starting positions, and a computable exact natural density is a motivated structural boundary for repetition theory, not an isolated short-length or arbitrary-slice calculation. The digit-product lemma can guide analogous analyses of non-balanced uniform morphisms.
